PROVENANCE OF THIS FIXTURE
==========================

READ THIS FIRST: MOST OF THE NUMBERS IN THIS DIRECTORY ARE SYNTHESISED.
They were never published by INE. They are test values, generated by a
formula, and they MUST NOT be quoted, charted, exported or cited as real
statistics anywhere outside this test fixture.

This directory is the golden export artifact the web test suite and local
`astro build` runs read (`web/src/lib/export/loader.ts`, `EXPORT_DIR`).
It is machine-generated output, never hand-edited -- the manifest's
sha256 digests are written by the real Go writer
(`app/internal/publishing/export.go`) and can be checked with
`sha256sum series/*.json`.

Follows the same convention as
`app/internal/ingestion/testdata/datos_serie/source.txt` and
`app/internal/adapters/ine/testdata/datos_serie/source.txt`, which
document the REAL captured payloads. The difference is exactly the point
of this file: those two directories hold real data, this one does not.


WHAT IS REAL HERE
-----------------

1. Every structural and metadata field: slugs, units, frequencies,
   decimals, source names, attribution strings, licence names and URLs,
   origin identifiers (EPA453100, EPA387796, IPC290751, IPC292511,
   CNTR6721, ECP320) and the schema shape. All of it comes from the
   shipped `/config` tree through the real pipeline.

2. The methodology breaks and the events. They are reconciled by the real
   `ingestion.ReconcileEditorialConfig` from `config/rupturas.yaml`,
   `config/eventos.yaml` and `config/gobiernos.yaml` -- the same editorial
   registries production reconciles.

3. THE NEWEST THREE OBSERVATIONS OF EVERY SERIES. Those rows are copied
   verbatim from the real, live-verified INE responses checked in under
   `app/internal/ingestion/testdata/datos_serie/` (fetched 2026-07-28; see
   that directory's own source.txt). So the "latest value" every indicator
   page renders IS a genuine published statistic:

     tasa-de-paro-epa      2025-Q4=9.93        2026-Q1=10.83     2026-Q2=9.87
     ocupados-epa          2025-Q4=22463.3     2026-Q1=22293.0   2026-Q2=22779.0
     ipc-general           2026-M04=102.883    2026-M05=102.951  2026-M06=103.598
     ipc-subyacente        2026-M04=102.672    2026-M05=102.911  2026-M06=103.339
     pib-cvi               2025-Q3=123.2859    2025-Q4=128.3448  2026-Q1=121.9959
     poblacion-residente   2025-Q4=49496923    2026-Q1=49590099  2026-Q2=49687120


WHAT IS SYNTHESISED HERE
------------------------

EVERY OTHER OBSERVATION. All the history preceding those three rows is
generated, not observed. It is not a capture, not an approximation of the
real historical series, and not a reconstruction of one. It exists so the
acceptance evidence (built pages, e2e traversal, transferred-bytes budget)
runs against a series as LONG as the real one instead of a 3-point stub.

The generated shape is deliberately a STRAIGHT LINE plus a fixed seasonal
offset. That choice is not laziness: real unemployment, inflation, GDP and
population histories are nothing like straight lines, so anyone who looks
at these charts can see at a glance that the history is not real. A
prettier, more realistic-looking curve would have been easy to produce and
far easier to mistake for the truth.

The exact recipe, for value number `i` (0-based) of a series with `N`
observations, where `T` is the value of the FIRST real tail row (the one
at index N-3):

    value(i) = round( startValue + (T - startValue) * i / (N - 3)
                      + seasonal[ordinal of i within its year] ,
                      decimals )

There is no randomness, no clock read and no external input anywhere in
that formula, so the fixture is byte-reproducible: regenerating it twice
yields identical files, digests included.

Per-series constants:

  slug                 N    span                        startValue   seasonal (by quarter / by month)
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  tasa-de-paro-epa     98   2002-Q1 .. 2026-Q2              11.50    +0.35  -0.20  -0.45  +0.30
  ocupados-epa         98   2002-Q1 .. 2026-Q2           16500.0     -150.0 +120.0 +200.0 -80.0
  ipc-general         294   2002-M01 .. 2026-M06            70.000   -0.30 -0.20 0.00 +0.20 +0.25 +0.30
                                                                     +0.10 +0.15 +0.05 +0.10 -0.05 -0.20
  ipc-subyacente      294   2002-M01 .. 2026-M06            72.000   -0.25 -0.15 0.00 +0.15 +0.20 +0.25
                                                                     +0.05 +0.10 +0.05 +0.10 -0.05 -0.15
  pib-cvi             125   1995-Q1 .. 2026-Q1              62.0000  -2.0   +0.5   0.0    +3.5
  poblacion-residente 122   1971-Q1 .. 2026-Q2           34000000     none

`N` and the span are each the series' REAL live length and real span,
recorded in openspec/changes/phase-1-indicator-page/apply-progress.md
(98 / 98 / 294 / 294 / 125 / 122). Only the VALUES inside that envelope
are invented; the shape of the envelope is real.

`poblacion-residente` walks the mixed cadence its own config declares
(`config/series/poblacion-residente.yaml`): Q1/Q3 only from 1971-Q1 to
2020-Q3, then every quarter from 2021-Q1. 100 semiannual points + 22
quarterly points = 122.

Every synthetic row is marked `Definitivo`. The real tail rows keep
whatever `T3_TipoDato` INE actually returned, which is why `pib-cvi` and
`poblacion-residente` end in `Provisional` points here -- they really do.

Every synthetic value stays inside the series' configured plausibility
bounds and period-over-period delta threshold
(`config/series/{slug}.yaml`, `validation.plausibility`), because the real
validation rules genuinely ran over this data: it was ingested through
`ingestion.IngestSeries`, not written into the artifact directly.


HOW IT WAS GENERATED
--------------------

Generated 2026-07-30 by a TEMPORARY generator,
`app/cmd/concontexto/zzgen_fullhistory_fixture_test.go`, deleted
immediately after running -- the same throwaway-generator convention
slices 3, 9a, 9b and 11 used (see apply-progress.md). It:

  1. started a testcontainers Postgres and ran the real migrations
     (`cmdMigrate up`);
  2. loaded the real embedded `/config` tree (`config.Load`);
  3. overrode exactly ONE field -- the `ine` source's `api.base_url` --
     to point at a local `httptest.Server` bound to the FIXED port 39935
     (fixed, not ephemeral, so the `origin.requestUrl` recorded in the
     artifact is stable and the fixture stays byte-reproducible);
  4. ran the real `ingest --reconcile` composition
     (`runIngestReconcile` -> `ingestion.ReconcileEditorialConfig`);
  5. ran the real `ingest --source=ine` composition (`runIngest` ->
     `ingestion.IngestSeries`), which published 294 / 294 / 98 / 125 /
     122 / 98 observations;
  6. ran the real `export --fixture` composition (`runExport` ->
     `buildExportDeps` -> `publishing.Export`) into this directory.

To rebuild it, restore a generator that does the above with the constants
in the table. Nothing here should ever be edited by hand.

The `http://127.0.0.1:39935/...` request URLs recorded in every series
document are that local fixture server -- another visible marker that this
artifact did not come from ine.es.
